scope: Spanish-language supplemental discovery only. This pass retains distribution identity while distinguishing derivatives, editions, releases, and the Linux kernel; no system records are created by this file.

candidates.reason: Argentine state educational GNU/Linux distribution. Educ.ar identifies it as a free operating system developed by EDUCAR Sociedad del Estado; it is a Debian-based distribution, not a separate kernel.
Argentine Debian-based GNU/Linux distribution developed by the Facultad de Informática of the Universidad Nacional de La Plata; no matching English-list manifest identity was found.
Argentine open-source distribution created at the Instituto de Diseño y Arte Cinematográfico for animation-oriented educational use; retain as a distribution identity rather than a new kernel.
Argentine GNU/Linux distribution associated with the Universidad Nacional de Salta. It is a distribution identity, not a separate operating-system kernel.
Defunct Argentine GNU/Linux distribution from Tucumán, based on Debian and Ubuntu. The identity is cataloged as a distribution, not as a replacement kernel or merely a LiveCD release.
Argentine radio-oriented GNU/Linux distribution derived from Canaima. Its derivative relationship is retained; it is not a release of Canaima itself.
Argentina-origin, artist and music-education oriented GNU/Linux distribution. It is a discontinued distribution lineage based on Knoppix, Kanotix, and Debian, not an independent kernel.
Argentine freedom-focused GNU/Linux distribution described as built without an earlier distribution base. It remains a GNU/Linux distribution identity, distinct from the Linux-libre kernel it uses.

Cuban GNU/Linux distribution developed at the Universidad de las Ciencias Informáticas by students and faculty for national free-software migration. Treat as a distribution, not a standalone operating-system family.

Venezuelan government GNU/Linux distribution based on Debian, used for public administration and education. Catalog as a distribution identity rather than conflating it with the Canaima Educativo deployment program.
Spanish free GNU/Linux distribution originally sponsored by the Universidad de Vigo. It is a distribution with Linux-libre, not the kernel itself.
An educational deployment and customized image of Canaima GNU/Linux for school laptops, rather than a separate operating-system identity.
The official Huayra history describes it as a version designed for Programa Conectar Igualdad Bonaerense; retain beneath Huayra rather than as a separate system.
